The 'GM', 'DEV', 'TEST' variants are PURE LUA-DEFINED CLASSES that wrap CommandDebuggerBase - they have no C++ TD, no C++ vftable, just registry-string entries. **The hypothesis that the 3 variants 'likely DO have C++ implementations' is FALSIFIED**. key_findings: **Only ONE C++ CommandDebugger class exists**: `Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::CommandDebuggerBase` (vftable 0x00FD510C, TD 0x012C0160). Full RTTI quartet present: vftable 0x00FD510C, COL 0x0115CF30, CHD 0x0115CF44, BCA 0x0115CF54, BCD-self 0x0115CF74, TD 0x012C0160.

**The GM/DEV/TEST variants are PURE LUA-DEFINED classes** - no C++ TD/vftable/CHD/BCA exist for them. They appear in the binary only as STRING LITERAL labels (s_CommandDebuggerGM_*, s_CommandDebuggerDEV_*, s_CommandDebuggerTEST_*) registered into the Lua class table by FUN_0078E3A0 (LuaClassRegistry BCS-Y-0398). Their implementations are Lua scripts that call into CommandDebuggerBase's C++ methods via the Lua-bridge.

**The GAP for the 3 user-mode variants is RESOLVED** - not a catalog completeness issue but a positive architectural finding. The pattern is: 1 C++ class (CommandDebuggerBase) + 3 Lua-defined wrappers (GM/DEV/TEST) that share the C++ implementation but differ in their Lua-side permission/feature scope. This is the same 'abstract Lua-bridge base' pattern identified for the 13 GAP class names (CommandDebuggerBaseClass, CommandDebuggerFUNCBaseClass, etc.) - extends that analysis to the 3 concrete user-mode variants which were misclassified as catalog candidates earlier.

**Architecture insight**: CommandDebuggerBase provides the debugger COMMAND IMPLEMENTATION; the 3 user-mode variants (GM = Game Master / DEV = Developer / TEST = Tester) are Lua-side PERMISSION-LEVEL WRAPPERS that gate which debug commands are accessible to which user roles. Each variant is a Lua class derived from CommandDebuggerBase via the `_defineClass` mechanism (per the findings on the Lua-bridge class system).

**CommandDebuggerBase ctor BCS-Y-1471 was cataloged earlier** but lacked vftable/TD cross-links - completes the class identity by adding the vftable + TD entries and amending the ctor with cross-references.

**The full Lua-bridge class registry has at least 36 classes** (per FUN_0078E3A0 enumeration) of which: 23 have C++ TDs (concrete C++ classes), 13 are abstract Lua-bridge bases (no C++ counterpart). The 3 GM/DEV/TEST 'concrete' variants are actually in the Lua-only bucket - bringing the GAP count to: 23 C++ concrete + 13 abstract Lua-bridge bases + 3 user-mode Lua wrappers = at least 39 classes (since FUN_0078E3A0 also registers some classes that may be Lua-only too).
